courses.title: Parametric Mounting Bracket
courses.objective: Build an L-bracket from fully dimensioned sketches: extrude, join, cut holes, fillet and chamfer.

steps.title: Dimensioned base sketch
instructions: Press K and pick the XY plane.
Draw a centred rectangle.
Dimension it 80 × 50 mm (Smart dimension, D).
steps.why: A sketch is the parametric seed: every later feature follows these two numbers.

checkpoint.expected: A closed, fully dimensioned 80 × 50 mm rectangle.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extrude the base plate
instructions: Extrude → choose Base sketch.
Distance 8 mm, operation New.
steps.why: Extrude turns the profile into a solid and records the distance as an editable number.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Upright wall sketch
instructions: Sketch on the XY plane offset 8 mm (top of the plate).
Rectangle 80 × 10 mm, back edge flush with the plate.
steps.why: Sketching on an offset plane places the next profile exactly on top of the plate.

checkpoint.expected: A rectangle on the top face along the back edge.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extrude and join the upright
instructions: Extrude the Upright sketch 40 mm.
Operation Join, so it merges into the plate.
steps.why: Join fuses the new volume with the existing body instead of creating a second one.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Cut the mounting holes
instructions: Sketch two circles Ø8 mm at (−28, −8) and (28, −8) on the plate top.
Extrude → Cut, 8 mm down.
steps.why: A cut extrude removes material. Both circles are dimensioned, so changing Ø updates both holes.

checkpoint.expected: Two through holes in the base plate.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Wizard hole in the upright
instructions: Part tab → Hole wizard, click the front face of the upright.
Simple hole Ø8, through all, moved 6 mm up from the face centre.
steps.why: The Hole wizard stores the hole as a feature you can re-size or move later.

checkpoint.expected: A hole through the upright wall.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Round the front corners
instructions: Select the two vertical corner edges of the base.
Fillet radius 4 mm.
steps.why: Fillets soften stress points and make the part safe to handle.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Chamfer the top edges
instructions: Select the two long top edges of the upright.
Chamfer distance 1.5 mm.
steps.why: A chamfer breaks the sharp edge and shows how edge features reference the solid.

checkpoint.expected: Finished bracket: one body, no errors.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Stepped Shaft with Keyway
courses.objective: Revolve a half-profile into a stepped shaft, then cut a keyway and break the edges.

steps.title: Half profile
instructions: Sketch on XY.
Draw the outline: Ø20 × 30, Ø30 × 45, Ø40 × 25 (radii 10 / 15 / 20) from the Y axis.
steps.why: Revolved parts are drawn as one half; the Y axis becomes the shaft centre line.

checkpoint.expected: A closed profile touching the Y axis.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Revolve 360°
instructions: Revolve → Profile = Shaft profile, axis Y, 360°.
steps.why: Revolve sweeps the profile around the axis, giving exact round steps.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Keyway sketch
instructions: Sketch on the XZ plane offset 35 mm.
Rectangle 8 × 6 mm centred above the Ø30 surface.
steps.why: The keyway is a small rectangle placed where the Ø30 section is.

checkpoint.expected: A small rectangle at the Ø30 section.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Cut the keyway
instructions: Extrude → Cut, 35 mm along the shaft.
steps.why: Cutting lengthwise creates the slot a key sits in.

checkpoint.expected: A keyway slot on the Ø30 section.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Break the end edges
instructions: Select the circular edge at the top end.
Chamfer 1.5 mm.
steps.why: Chamfered ends make assembly easier and protect the part.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Bearing Housing
courses.objective: Model a flanged bearing housing: boss, bore, counterbore, mounting holes, ribs and fillets.

steps.title: Base plate
instructions: Sketch a centred 100 × 60 rectangle on XY.
Extrude 12 mm.
steps.why: Start with the footprint that will bolt to the machine.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Round boss
instructions: Sketch a Ø60 circle on the plate top.
Extrude 28 mm, Join.
steps.why: The boss carries the bearing; its height sets the seat length.

checkpoint.expected: A cylindrical boss on the plate.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Bore for the bearing
instructions: Sketch a Ø35 circle on the boss top (offset 40).
Extrude → Cut 40 mm.
steps.why: The bore diameter is the bearing outside diameter.

checkpoint.expected: A Ø35 hole through the boss and plate.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Counterbore seat
instructions: Sketch a Ø44 circle on the boss top.
Cut 6 mm deep.
steps.why: A stepped seat lets the bearing locate against a shoulder.

checkpoint.expected: A shallow wider seat at the top.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Four mounting holes
instructions: Sketch four Ø10 circles at (±40, ±22).
Cut through the plate.
steps.why: Symmetric hole positions keep the pattern easy to edit.

checkpoint.expected: Four holes in the plate corners.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Stiffening ribs
instructions: Sketch two thin rectangles (76 × 6 and 6 × 48) crossing at the centre.
Extrude both 18 mm, Join.
steps.why: Ribs add stiffness without much material.

checkpoint.expected: Two crossing ribs around the boss.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Fillet the plate corners
instructions: Select the four vertical plate corners.
Fillet 8 mm.
steps.why: Rounded corners are safer and look finished.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Pipe Flange, 8 Bolts
courses.objective: Build a pipe flange: disk, hub, bore and an 8-hole bolt circle.

steps.title: Flange disk
instructions: Sketch a Ø140 circle on XY.
Extrude 16 mm.
steps.why: The disk is the sealing face of the flange.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Hub
instructions: Sketch Ø76 on the disk top.
Extrude 38 mm, Join.
steps.why: The hub supports the pipe weld and adds stiffness.

checkpoint.expected: A hub on top of the disk.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pipe bore
instructions: Sketch Ø50 on the hub top.
Cut through everything (54 mm).
steps.why: The bore matches the pipe inside diameter.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Raised sealing face
instructions: Sketch two concentric circles, Ø124 and Ø92, on the disk top.
Extrude 2 mm, Join.
steps.why: A raised face concentrates gasket pressure on a narrow ring, as on real ASME flanges.

checkpoint.expected: A thin raised ring around the hub.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Bolt circle
instructions: Sketch 8 circles Ø12 on a Ø110 bolt circle, every 45°, on top of the raised face.
Cut 18 mm so the holes pass through ring and disk.
steps.why: A bolt circle spaces the holes evenly around the axis.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Boolean Workflow: Union, Subtract, Intersect
courses.objective: Combine primitive solids with union, subtract and intersect to make a machined block.

steps.title: Target block
instructions: Model → Box.
Width 80, depth 60, height 30, at the origin.
steps.why: The first body is the target the others modify.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Cylinder tool
instructions: Model → Cylinder.
Radius 14, height 50, base at z = −10 so it passes through.
steps.why: A tool body must overlap the target to change it.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Subtract
instructions: Select the block first, then the cylinder.
Combine → Subtract.
steps.why: Subtract removes the tool volume from the target.

checkpoint.expected: A round hole through the block.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Boss with Union
instructions: Create a second box 30 × 20 × 24 overlapping the top.
Select block then box → Union.
steps.why: Union merges bodies into one solid.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Round the shape with Intersect
instructions: Create a sphere radius 52 centred at z = 10.
Select block then sphere → Intersect.
steps.why: Intersect keeps only the volume the two bodies share.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Shelled Electronics Enclosure
courses.objective: Create an enclosure: rounded blank, shell, screw bosses, screw holes and a connector opening.

steps.title: Outer blank
instructions: Sketch a 120 × 80 rectangle.
Extrude 35 mm.
steps.why: Model the outside first, then hollow it.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Round the vertical corners
instructions: Select the four vertical edges.
Fillet 8 mm.
steps.why: Rounding before the shell makes a uniform wall.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Shell with open top
instructions: Shell → click the top face.
Wall thickness 2.5 mm.
steps.why: Shell hollows the part and leaves the chosen face open.

checkpoint.expected: A hollow enclosure with an open top.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Screw bosses
instructions: Sketch four Ø10 circles near the corners on the inside floor.
Extrude 12 mm, Join.
steps.why: Bosses give the screws something solid to bite into.

checkpoint.expected: Four cylinders standing on the floor.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Screw pilot holes
instructions: Sketch Ø3.2 circles in the boss centres.
Cut 10 mm down.
steps.why: Pilot holes size the thread for M3 self-tapping screws.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Connector opening
instructions: Sketch a 24 × 12 rectangle on the YZ plane at the right wall.
Cut through the wall only.
steps.why: A symmetric cut limited to the wall thickness opens one side.

checkpoint.expected: A rectangular opening in the side wall.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: NURBS Surface Fundamentals
courses.objective: Build a curved NURBS sheet from section curves, then control its CV grid, knots and splits.

steps.title: Three section curves
instructions: Sketch three fit-point splines on parallel XZ planes at Y = 0, 30 and 60.
Give each a gentle wave.
steps.why: Sections are the curves the surface will pass through.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft a NURBS sheet
instructions: NURBS → Loft: pick the three sections.
Degree 3 across the sections.
steps.why: A loft blends smoothly through all sections.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rebuild to a clean grid
instructions: NURBS → Rebuild: 7 × 7 control points, degree 3 × 3.
steps.why: Rebuild gives a predictable control-point grid you can edit.

checkpoint.expected: A sheet with a regular 7 × 7 CV grid.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add a knot
instructions: NURBS → Add knot: direction U, at 0.5.
steps.why: Inserting a knot adds CVs without changing the shape.

checkpoint.expected: Shape unchanged, one more CV row.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Split the surface
instructions: NURBS → Split: direction U at 0.5.
steps.why: Splitting is exact: both halves keep the original shape.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Lift one half
instructions: NURBS → Transform: move Z +12.
steps.why: Moving whole surfaces is how you assemble a model from patches.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Revolved NURBS Vase
courses.objective: Draw a spline profile, revolve it, change the revolve angle, then thicken into a solid vase.

steps.title: Profile curve
instructions: Sketch a fit-point spline on XZ from the foot to the mouth.
X is radius, Y is height.
steps.why: The profile is the whole design: change it and the vase changes.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Revolve
instructions: NURBS → Revolve+: axis Y, 360°, smooth.
steps.why: A revolved NURBS surface is exact and smooth.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Preview a cut-away
instructions: Edit Vase surface → angle 270°.
steps.why: Parameters stay editable — try any angle.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Back to 360°
instructions: Set the angle back to 360°.
steps.why: Restoring the angle shows the history is live.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken to a solid
instructions: NURBS → Thicken: 3 mm.
steps.why: Thicken turns the surface into a solid with wall thickness.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Lofted Five-Section Bottle
courses.objective: Control a bottle with five section circles at different heights, then thicken it.

steps.title: Base section
instructions: Sketch a Ø44 circle on XY.
steps.why: Each section sets the size at one height.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Body sections
instructions: Sketch Ø60 at Z = 25 and Ø62 at Z = 60.
steps.why: Two similar sections hold the body straight.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Shoulder and neck
instructions: Sketch Ø28 at Z = 85 and Ø18 at Z = 104.
steps.why: Closer, smaller sections make the shoulder turn.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft all five
instructions: NURBS → Loft: select the five sections in order.
steps.why: Section order defines the surface direction.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken
instructions: NURBS → Thicken 2 mm.
steps.why: A wall turns the surface into a manufacturable body.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Swept Handle and Tapered Pipe
courses.objective: Create a handle by sweeping a profile along a path, then a tapered pipe along the same path.

steps.title: Path curve
instructions: Sketch a fit-point spline on XY.
steps.why: The path is the centre line of the handle.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Profile
instructions: Sketch a Ø12 circle on XZ at the path start.
steps.why: The profile is the cross-section.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Sweep
instructions: NURBS → Sweep: profile = Handle profile, path = Handle path.
steps.why: Sweep drags the profile along the path.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Taper
instructions: Create another sweep with end scale 0.4.
steps.why: End scale tapers the section along the path.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pipe tool
instructions: NURBS → Pipe: radius 10 → 3 along the path.
steps.why: Pipe is the fast way to make a round section that changes size.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Project a Curve onto a Surface
courses.objective: Project a sketch spline onto a curved sheet to create a curve on the surface.

steps.title: Curved sheet
instructions: Sketch three splines on XZ at Y = −35, 0, 35.
NURBS → Loft them into a sheet.
steps.why: A curved host for the projection.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Design curve above
instructions: Sketch a spline on a plane 30 mm above the sheet.
steps.why: The curve describes where the feature should go.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Project down
instructions: NURBS+ → Project: curve onto the sheet, direction −Z.
steps.why: The result lies exactly on the surface.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Trim, Untrim and Retrim
courses.objective: Understand the difference between the underlying NURBS surface and its trimmed boundary.

steps.title: Base surface
instructions: Loft the curved sheet.
steps.why: Trimming never changes the surface underneath.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Trim curve
instructions: Sketch a Ø40 circle on XY.
steps.why: The trim boundary is any closed curve.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Trim inside
instructions: NURBS+ → Trim: keep outside.
steps.why: The kept region has a circular opening.

checkpoint.expected: A sheet with a round hole.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Untrim
instructions: NURBS+ → Untrim: all.
steps.why: Untrim restores the full surface.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Retrim, keep inside
instructions: Trim again with keep inside.
steps.why: Same curve, opposite region.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: N-Sided Fill
courses.objective: Fill a five-sided boundary with a single smooth surface and tune its tension.

steps.title: Pentagon boundary
instructions: Sketch a regular pentagon, radius 40.
steps.why: A closed boundary is all N-sided fill needs.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Fill
instructions: NURBS+ → N-sided: pick the boundary, mode flat.
steps.why: The fill is built from several patches that meet smoothly.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Increase tension
instructions: Edit the fill: tension 2.5.
steps.why: Tension controls how stiff the interior is.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Free mode
instructions: Edit the fill: mode free.
steps.why: Free mode relaxes the interior.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: G0 → G1 → G2 → G3 Surface Matching
courses.objective: Match two surfaces through position, tangent, curvature and third-order continuity and inspect each result.

steps.title: Surface A
instructions: Loft and rebuild surface A with 8 × 8 control points.
steps.why: G2 and G3 matching need at least 4 control rows across the edge.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Surface B with a gap and angle
instructions: Loft and rebuild surface B 10 mm away and tilted upward.
steps.why: The deliberate mismatch is what you will repair.

checkpoint.expected: Two surfaces with a visible gap.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G0 — position
instructions: NURBS+ → Match: B to A, continuity G0.
steps.why: G0 closes the gap: the edges meet, but a crease remains.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G1 — tangent
instructions: Edit Match → G1.
steps.why: G1 also matches the tangent plane: no visible crease.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G2 — curvature
instructions: Edit Match → G2.
steps.why: G2 matches curvature across the join, so reflections flow.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G3 — change of curvature
instructions: Edit Match → G3.
steps.why: G3 matches how fast the curvature changes: the highest quality join.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Inspect with curvature comb and zebra
instructions: NURBS+ → Comb and Zebra.
steps.why: Combs and zebra stripes make tiny continuity errors visible.

checkpoint.expected: Comb and zebra stripes visible on the join.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: G0 → G3 Blend Between Two Surfaces
courses.objective: Create a transition surface between two separated sheets at increasing continuity.

steps.title: Surface A
instructions: Loft and rebuild surface A.
steps.why: Blends need clean edges to attach to.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Surface B
instructions: Loft and rebuild surface B across the gap.
steps.why: The gap is what the blend will fill.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G0 blend
instructions: NURBS+ → Blend: edge A-u1 to B-u0, G0 both sides.
steps.why: G0 only meets the edges.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G1 blend
instructions: Edit Blend → G1 both sides.
steps.why: G1 matches tangents.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G2 blend
instructions: Edit Blend → G2 both sides.
steps.why: G2 matches curvature.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G3 blend
instructions: Edit Blend → G3 both sides, tangent strength 1.3.
steps.why: G3 plus a fuller blend shape gives a premium-quality transition.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the join
instructions: NURBS+ → Zebra.
steps.why: Straight, continuous zebra stripes confirm the quality.

checkpoint.expected: Zebra stripes flow across the blend.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Curvature Comb, Zebra and Deviation
courses.objective: Use the three analysis tools to find and fix a poor transition.

steps.title: A rough transition
instructions: Build A and B and join them with a G0 match.
steps.why: G0 leaves a curvature jump.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Curvature comb
instructions: NURBS+ → Comb.
steps.why: The comb needles jump at the join, which is the problem.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Zebra stripes
instructions: NURBS+ → Zebra.
steps.why: Stripes break at the join.

checkpoint.expected: Zebra stripes kinked at the join.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Fix with G2
instructions: Edit the Match → G2.
steps.why: The comb now flows continuously.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Deviation check
instructions: NURBS+ → Deviation.
steps.why: Deviation shows the shape moved by the fix.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Master: Perfume Flacon with G3 Collar
courses.objective: A full multi-surface product: lofted glass body, revolved neck and cap, a swept collar ring, a G3 blend, base plate and an offset liquid surface.

steps.title: Body sections
instructions: Sketch four rectangles: 46×30 at Z=0, 54×36 at Z=26, 50×32 at Z=54 and 26×18 at Z=72.
steps.why: The tapered rectangles define a modern flat-sided flacon.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the glass body
instructions: NURBS → Loft: pick the four sections.
steps.why: Loft blends the four sections into one body.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Neck profile
instructions: Sketch a short spline on XZ from the shoulder up.
steps.why: The neck is a revolved profile.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Straight 3D route
instructions: Model → 3D sketch.
Click points, then type the exact X, Y, Z values in the table: (0,0,0), (80,0,0), (80,60,0), (80,60,50), (0,60,50).
steps.why: A 3D sketch holds points in space, not on one plane.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Spline through space
instructions: Draw a second 3D sketch and set its mode to Spline.
steps.why: Splines flow smoothly through every point.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rebuild as a clean NURBS curve
instructions: NURBS+ → Rebuild curve: 8 control points, degree 3.
steps.why: A rebuilt curve has fewer, evenly spread control points.

checkpoint.expected: A rebuilt curve beside the spline.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Project Edges to a Cover Plate
courses.objective: Project the outline and holes of a part onto a plane and extrude a matching cover.

steps.title: Base plate
instructions: Model → Box 80 × 50 × 10.
steps.why: The part whose outline you will reuse.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Two holes
instructions: Part → Hole wizard twice: Ø12 at (18, 8) and Ø8 at (−20, −10).
steps.why: Holes will be projected as real circles.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Project the top edges
instructions: Model → Project edges: select the top outline and both hole edges.
Target plane XY offset 25 mm.
steps.why: Projected geometry stays linked to the solid.

checkpoint.expected: A sketch 25 mm above with outline and holes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extrude the cover
instructions: Extrude the projected sketch 3 mm.
steps.why: The cover follows the plate: change a hole and it updates.

checkpoint.expected: A matching cover plate floating above.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: 3D Pipe Run
courses.objective: Route a pipe in space with a 3D sketch and turn the route into a mitred pipe run.

steps.title: Route layout
steps.why: The centre line decides every bend.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add a branch
steps.why: Branches are separate curves that meet the main run.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pipe the main run
instructions: Part+ → Weldment: Round tube Ø48.3 × 3.2, mitred corners.
steps.why: The weldment tool sweeps a standard profile along each segment.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pipe the branch
instructions: Weldment again for the branch: Ø33.7 × 3.2.
steps.why: Different sizes for different branches.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Spatial Weldment Frame
courses.objective: Lay out a table frame in one 3D sketch and build it as mitred square-tube members.

steps.title: Top rails
instructions: 3D sketch, closed rectangle at Z = 720: 900 × 520.
steps.why: The top frame is one closed loop.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Legs
instructions: Four vertical lines from Z = 0 to Z = 720 at the corners.
steps.why: One sketch can hold many members.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Lower shelf rails
instructions: A second closed rectangle at Z = 140.
steps.why: A lower shelf stiffens the legs.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Weld the top and legs
instructions: Part+ → Weldment: Square tube 40 × 40 × 3 for the top and for the legs.
steps.why: Standard profiles come with real dimensions and a cut list.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Weld the shelf
instructions: Weldment: Square tube 30 × 30 × 3 for the shelf rails.
steps.why: Lighter tube for the lower shelf.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Image Trace to Editable Sketch
courses.objective: Trace a picture into sketch geometry (outline, holes, star cut-out) and extrude it.

steps.title: Trace the badge picture
instructions: Model → Image trace: load the picture, width 104 mm.
Aakar finds the outline, four holes, a star cut-out and an island.
steps.why: Tracing converts pixels into real sketch geometry.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extrude 4 mm
instructions: Extrude the traced sketch 4 mm.
steps.why: Because the geometry is real, you can extrude, dimension and edit it.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rescale the trace
instructions: Edit the Trace feature: width 130 mm.
steps.why: The trace is parametric: change the width and the sketch and solid follow.

checkpoint.expected: A larger badge with identical proportions.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: 3D Curve Network to Surface
courses.objective: Draw a grid of 3D curves and build one smooth surface through all of them.

steps.title: Direction-1 curves
instructions: 3D sketch: three splines along X at Y = −30, 0, 30.
steps.why: Each curve is a section of the final surface.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Direction-2 curves
instructions: 3D sketch: three splines along Y at X = −40, 0, 40, meeting the first three.
steps.why: They must cross the first family exactly.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Network surface
instructions: NURBS+ → Network: three curves per direction.
steps.why: The surface interpolates the whole grid.

checkpoint.expected: A smooth surface through the grid.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Inner skin
instructions: NURBS → Offset: −2 mm, keep the original.
steps.why: An offset copy gives the shell its second wall.

checkpoint.expected: A second surface under the first.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Master: Tubular Chassis from One Skeleton
courses.objective: Draw a complete tubular chassis skeleton in 3D sketches and build it with mitred tube members of different sizes.

steps.title: Floor frame
instructions: 3D sketch: closed rectangle 700 × 1400 at Z = 0.
steps.why: The floor loop is the foundation.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Cross members
instructions: Three straight lines across the frame at Y = 350, 700, 1050.
steps.why: Cross members add torsional stiffness.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Roll hoops
instructions: Two U-shaped hoops, 420 mm high, at Y = 420 and Y = 980.
steps.why: Hoops form the cabin cage.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Roof rails
instructions: Two lines joining the tops of the hoops.
steps.why: Roof rails tie the hoops together.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Diagonal braces
instructions: Diagonals from floor to roof on both sides.
steps.why: Triangulation makes the cage rigid.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Weld the floor
instructions: Part+ → Weldment: Rectangular tube 50 × 30 × 3 for the floor and cross members.
steps.why: Heavier tube in the floor.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Weld the cage
instructions: Weldment: Square tube 40 × 40 × 3 for hoops and roof rails.
steps.why: Same profile for the cage.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Weld the braces
instructions: Weldment: Square tube 30 × 30 × 3 for the diagonals.
steps.why: Lighter tubes for secondary members.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Dragon-Scale Vase
courses.objective: Cover a vase with overlapping, downward-pointing scales: the new Scales pattern, its lean, depth and density.

steps.title: Profile
steps.learn: A barrel profile shows the overlapping scales well.
instructions: Model › Sketch on XZ.
Draw an open spline from foot to mouth.
steps.why: Scales look best on a vase with a clear belly.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Start from diamonds
steps.learn: Scales are a variation of the diamond pattern, so start there.
instructions: NURBS › Faceted: Diamond, 14 around, 9 rows, depth 4.
steps.why: Knowing the plain pattern first makes the scale lean easy to see.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Switch to Scales
steps.learn: The Scales pattern tilts each facet’s peak downward, like a roof tile.
instructions: Double-click the vase.
Pattern Scales (staggered, pointing down).
steps.why: Overlap comes from the lean, not from extra geometry.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Stronger overlap
steps.learn: Scale lean is how far the peak slides toward the lower corner.
instructions: Scale lean 0.8, depth 5, 16 around, 12 rows.
steps.why: Lean 0 equals the diamond pattern; around 0.8 reads as dragon scales.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Finer scales
steps.learn: More rows and columns make smaller scales, like a fish.
instructions: 26 around, 20 rows, depth 3, lean 0.65.
steps.why: Scale size should follow the object size: smaller scales read as fish, larger as dragon.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Reshape the body
steps.learn: The scales follow the profile.
instructions: Double-click “Vase profile”.
Fuller belly, narrower mouth.
steps.why: Every scale is regenerated, so you never edit them one by one.

checkpoint.expected: The same scale pattern on a rounder vase.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Wall and base
steps.learn: Set the hollow shell thickness.
instructions: Wall 2.5 mm, base 5 mm.
steps.why: Pointed scales add volume, so keep the wall thin.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Back to bumps
steps.learn: Lean 0 returns to diamonds: the same feature, the same inputs.
instructions: Scale lean 0.
steps.why: One feature with a few switches covers a whole family of textures.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Choose and export
steps.learn: Set the look you like and export it.
instructions: Scale lean 0.7, then Model › Mesh check and 3MF.
steps.why: A faceted solid is already printable.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Parameter-Driven Vase
courses.objective: Drive a vase from two global parameters, width and height, so that one number resizes it and re-counts its flutes.

steps.title: Define the parameters
steps.learn: Global parameters are named numbers any feature can use. Here: a width and a height.
instructions: Model › Parameters.
Add W = 60 and H = 150.
steps.why: Naming the key dimensions is the first step of every parametric design.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: A derived parameter
steps.learn: Parameters can use other parameters. Add a flute count that grows with the width.
instructions: Add FL = round(W/6).
steps.why: A formula turns one input into several consistent outputs.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Profile
steps.learn: A unit-scale profile that the vase will scale.
instructions: Model › Sketch on XZ.
Draw a spline: radius 30 at the belly, 150 tall.
steps.why: The shape is drawn once at a known size; the parameters scale it.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: The vase
steps.learn: A normal parametric vase for now.
instructions: NURBS › Vase: pick the profile.
Flutes 10, depth 0.08, twist 60°.
steps.why: Start with plain numbers, then replace them with expressions.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Link the radius to W
steps.learn: Typing =W/60 in a dimension box links it to the parameter.
instructions: Select the vase, open Dimensions.
Radius scale: =W/60.
steps.why: A linked value shows in blue and follows the parameter.

checkpoint.expected: Radius scale is now driven by W.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Link the height to H
steps.learn: The same for the height scale.
instructions: Height scale: =H/150.
steps.why: Both numbers now come from named, meaningful parameters.

checkpoint.expected: Height scale is driven by H.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Link the flutes to FL
steps.learn: Flute count comes from the derived parameter.
instructions: Flutes: =FL.
steps.why: Chains of parameters keep related dimensions consistent.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Change one number
steps.learn: Set the width to 90. The whole vase is rebuilt.
instructions: Parameters panel: W = 90.
steps.why: The scale grows to 1.5, FL becomes 15, and the vase re-counts its flutes by itself.

checkpoint.expected: A wider vase with more flutes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Make it tall and slim
steps.learn: Change both numbers.
steps.why: This is the point of a parametric model: a few numbers control the whole shape.

checkpoint.expected: A tall, slim vase with 7 flutes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the links
steps.learn: See what drives what.
instructions: Open Parameters and look at the Linked values table.
steps.why: Always keep a record of which values are driven by which parameters.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Second vase from the same parameters
steps.learn: Link another vase to the same parameters, with a different offset.
instructions: Add a second vase with pos X 150, link scale =W/60*0.8.
steps.why: Reusing parameters keeps a whole collection in step.

checkpoint.expected: A second vase that follows W and H at 80 %.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Save
steps.learn: Parameters are saved with the project.
instructions: File › Save.
steps.why: Reopen the file and change W to see everything rebuild.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Vase Family from One Master Profile
courses.objective: Draw one profile curve, build three different vases from it, then edit the profile once and watch every vase follow.

steps.title: Master profile
steps.learn: Every vase in this family reads the same curve. Change it later and all of them update.
instructions: Open a project and choose Model › Sketch on the XZ plane.
Draw a fit-point spline from the foot (small radius) up to the mouth.
X is the radius, Y is the height.
steps.why: One shared profile means one place to change the shape of the whole collection.

checkpoint.expected: An open spline, about 150 mm tall, wider in the middle.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vase A: twisted flutes
steps.learn: A parametric vase turns the profile into a NURBS surface and then modulates it with flutes and a twist.
instructions: NURBS › Vase: pick “Vase profile”.
Flutes 10, depth 0.08, sharpness 1.5, twist 60°.
steps.why: Flutes, twist and sharpness are plain numbers you can edit at any time.

checkpoint.expected: A fluted surface with a gentle spiral.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vase B: smooth and small
steps.learn: Setting flutes to 0 gives a smooth surface of revolution, here scaled to 80 %.
instructions: Create a second vase from the same profile.
Flutes 0, scale 0.8, height scale 0.8, position X 140.
steps.why: Scale and position let you build a set without drawing anything new.

checkpoint.expected: A second, smaller, smooth vase to the right.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vase C: crystal
steps.learn: High sharpness makes the flutes crisp, and a negative twist spirals the other way.
instructions: Third vase: flutes 6, depth 0.14, sharpness 4, twist −90°.
Scale 0.7, height scale 1.25, position X −125.
steps.why: Sharpness 1 is soft and wavy, 4 is faceted like cut glass.

checkpoint.expected: A tall, crisp, spiralling vase on the left.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Edit the master profile once
steps.learn: Because all three vases reference one sketch, editing it updates the whole family at the same time.
instructions: Double-click “Vase profile” in the feature list.
Move the belly point out and the mouth point in.
Finish the sketch and watch all three vases change.
steps.why: This is what parametric means: the shape lives in one place, and everything derived from it is rebuilt.

checkpoint.expected: All three vases now have fuller bellies and narrower mouths.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Tune one vase only
steps.learn: Each vase also has its own numbers. Changing them affects that vase alone.
instructions: Double-click “Vase A”.
Flutes 8, twist 120°, depth 0.06.
steps.why: Shared inputs (profile) and private inputs (flutes, twist) are what make a family.

checkpoint.expected: Vase A has a tighter spiral; B and C are unchanged.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add a fourth member
steps.learn: A new vase costs one dialog, because the profile already exists.
instructions: NURBS › Vase again, same profile.
Flutes 8, depth 0.1, sharpness 2.5, twist 0, scale 0.55, position Y −110.
steps.why: Designing a product range is mostly choosing different numbers for the same shapes.

checkpoint.expected: A small vase in front of the group.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken the hero vase
steps.learn: A surface has no thickness. Thicken offsets it into a closed solid you can export or print. Thicken cost grows quickly with the number of sections, so lower them first.
instructions: Double-click “Vase A”: sections around 36, rows 12.
NURBS › Thicken: choose “Vase A · twisted flutes”, thickness 2.4 mm, density 3.
steps.why: A closed, valid solid is what STL, 3MF and STEP exports need. 36 × 12 sections keep 8 flutes clean and thicken in a few seconds.

checkpoint.expected: A solid wall of 2.4 mm on vase A.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Save and reuse
steps.learn: Save the project. Next time, change the profile and every vase follows.
instructions: File › Save.
Optional: Model › 3MF to export the thick vase for 3D printing.
steps.why: Keeping the design as history, not as a mesh, is what lets you come back and edit it.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Twisted Fluted Vase to Printable Solid
courses.objective: Tune flutes, twist and sharpness on one vase, then thicken it into a printable solid and check it.

steps.title: Profile
steps.learn: A simple tall profile shows off the twist best.
instructions: Model › Sketch on XZ.
Fit-point spline from foot to mouth.
steps.why: The profile decides the silhouette; the flutes only add relief.

checkpoint.expected: A slim, slightly bulging profile 160 mm tall.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Smooth vase first
steps.learn: Start with no flutes so you can see the plain shape.
instructions: NURBS › Vase.
Flutes 0.
steps.why: Build in stages: a smooth base first, then add relief.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add flutes
steps.learn: Eight flutes at a shallow depth.
instructions: Double-click the vase.
Flutes 8, depth 0.07.
steps.why: Depth is a fraction of the local radius, so the flutes scale with the vase.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Add a quarter twist
steps.learn: Twist turns the flutes as they climb.
instructions: Twist 90°.
steps.why: Twist is total rotation over the full height.

checkpoint.expected: The flutes spiral by a quarter turn.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Sharpen the edges
steps.learn: Sharpness 1 is soft, 4 is crisp.
instructions: Sharpness 3.
steps.why: Crisp flutes catch light and read as cut glass.

checkpoint.expected: The flute ridges are now crisp.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Deeper flutes
steps.learn: Increase depth for a stronger relief.
instructions: Depth 0.12.
steps.why: More relief means thicker material is needed later, so watch the wall thickness.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Reverse the spiral
steps.learn: A negative twist reverses the direction.
instructions: Twist −140°.
steps.why: Handedness is a design choice: pair a left and a right twist for a matching set.

checkpoint.expected: The spiral now runs the other way.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Choose the section count
steps.learn: More sections give a smoother surface, but Thicken time grows quickly with them. 36 around × 12 rows is a good balance for 8 flutes.
instructions: Double-click the vase.
Sections around 36, rows 12.
steps.why: Decide the resolution before the expensive step, not after it.

checkpoint.expected: The surface is slightly coarser but still crisp.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken to a solid
steps.learn: Offset the surface by the wall thickness to get a closed solid.
instructions: NURBS › Thicken: pick the vase, thickness 2.2 mm, density 3.
steps.why: A 2 mm wall prints well in most materials.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the mesh
steps.learn: Mesh check reports open or non-manifold edges and the volume.
instructions: Select the solid.
Model › Mesh check.
steps.why: A printable model must be a closed shell with no open edges.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Export for printing
steps.learn: 3MF keeps millimetres and colours.
instructions: Model › 3MF.
Open the file in your slicer.
steps.why: Always preview the first layers in the slicer before printing.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Egg-Core Vase Gallery
courses.objective: Shape three egg-form vases with bias, foot cut, mouth cut and scale, then thicken one.

steps.title: One egg
steps.learn: The egg core is a closed-form profile defined by five numbers; no sketch is needed.
instructions: NURBS › Egg core.
Max radius 62, height 190, bias 0.12.
steps.why: Bias moves the widest point up or down, which is what makes it egg-shaped.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Slimmer, taller egg
steps.learn: Same tool, different numbers.
instructions: Max radius 48, height 230, bias 0.2.
Position X 150.
steps.why: You can read a lot about the shape just from the radius-to-height ratio.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Wide bowl
steps.learn: A negative bias moves the belly low.
instructions: Max radius 80, height 140, bias −0.15.
Position X −170.
steps.why: Negative bias gives a bowl or a pear shape.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Foot cut
steps.learn: Foot cut trims the bottom so the vase stands on a flat base.
instructions: Double-click Egg 1.
Foot cut 0.14.
steps.why: A flat foot is what stops a round vase from rolling.

checkpoint.expected: Egg 1 now stands on a wider foot.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Mouth cut
steps.learn: Mouth cut sets the opening.
instructions: Double-click Egg 2.
Mouth cut 0.8.
steps.why: A smaller opening suits stems; a wider one suits fruit.

checkpoint.expected: A narrower mouth on the tall egg.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Scale the group
steps.learn: Scale resizes a vase without touching its proportions.
instructions: Double-click Egg 3.
Radius scale 1.15.
steps.why: Scale keeps proportions; radius and height change them.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken one egg
steps.learn: Offset Egg 1 into a solid.

courses.title: Bottle, Cap and Thread (sketch-based, print tolerance, section check)
courses.objective: Build a 3D-printable screw-top bottle the conventional way: revolve the bottle and cap about their sketch axis lines, SKETCH a dimensioned thread tooth referenced to that axis, sweep it along a helix on both parts, repeat the grip flutes with Pattern+, control the fit with one clearance parameter, then seat the cap and prove the fit with a coloured, outlined section view.

steps.title: Plan the parts and the print tolerance
instructions: Bottle: Ø60 × 128 mm, 2 mm wall. Neck core Ø20.8, thread major Ø24, pitch 3 mm, right-hand, 5 turns.
Cap: Ø31 × 22.5 mm, bore Ø24, internal thread of the same pitch and hand, 4 turns.
Thread tooth (sketched, not a tool): 60° flanks, 1.6 mm deep, 2.25 mm wide at the root, 0.4 mm flat at the crest.
Tolerance: one global parameter clr = 0.15 mm. Both threads shrink by clr on every side, so the printed bolt and nut never touch (0.15 – 0.30 mm for FDM, 0.10 for resin).
Facets: set Settings › Arc / curve facets to 48 so round walls and threads are smooth enough for a 0.1 mm clearance to mean something (32 facets would eat about 0.06 mm of it, 48 about 0.03).

Referencing rule used in every sketch: sketch (0,0) is the part origin, X = radius from the axis, Y = height, and the AXIS is a dashed amber construction line, always the first line you draw, so it is named L1. Turn Names on (the “Aa” tool in the sketch, or the “Aa” button under the view cube in the model) to see L1, L2 … on every line.
steps.why: A screw closure only works if both threads share size, pitch and hand, and if the clearance is deliberate. Decide the numbers first; every later sketch is dimensioned from the same origin and the same axis line.

checkpoint.expected: Global parameter clr = 0.15 exists and the numbers are written down.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

build.note: Thread M24 × 3, tooth 1.6 deep, tolerance clr = 0.15 mm

steps.title: Bottle wall profile (with its axis line L1)
instructions: Press K and pick the XZ plane (sketch X = radius, sketch Y = height).
FIRST draw the axis: a construction line from (0,0) to (0,128) (toggle the dashed Construction tool, then Line). It becomes L1.
Then ONE closed outline of the wall, (radius, height): (0,0) → (25,0) → 5 mm corner arc → (30,5) → (30,78).
Shoulder: S-curve from (30,78) to (10.4,104), 10-segment polyline, r = 20.2 + 9.8·cos(π·(z − 78)/26).
Neck: (10.4,104) → (10.4,128) → (8,128) → (8,104); inner shoulder 2 mm in at the body and 2.4 mm at the neck, back to (28,78); inside wall (28,78) → (28,8) → 5 mm arc → (23,3) → (0,3) → (0,0).
steps.why: The neck is drawn at the thread's MINOR radius (10.4). The thread tooth is added on top of this plain core, so the core stays an exact cylinder. The construction axis line is what the Revolve (and later the thread) turns about.

checkpoint.expected: A closed wall outline plus a dashed amber axis line along X = 0 (named L1).

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Revolve the bottle about its axis line
instructions: Revolve → Profile = Bottle wall profile.
Axis = L1 · construction line (the list shows every line by the same name the sketch shows). While the dialog is open the model draws the axis in cyan and labels it.
Angle 360°, operation New.
steps.why: Choosing the sketch's own axis line (instead of a global X/Y) ties the bottle, and later the thread, to one visible reference.

checkpoint.expected: One hollow bottle, 128 mm tall, with a smooth Ø20.8 neck. It is coloured blue.

steps.title: Sketch the bottle thread tooth (referenced to the axis)
instructions: Sketch on the XZ plane again.

Draw the construction guides first: the AXIS line (0,106) → (0,116) [L1], the root line at r = 10.4 [L2], the crest line at r = 12 [L3], and two horizontal centre lines at z = 109.5 [L4, start] and z = 112.5 [L5, next turn].

Dimension it from the origin: 10.4 and 12 (radii from the axis), 109.5 (height of the start centre line), 3 (pitch between the centre lines), then 0.6 tail, 1.6 depth, 0.4 crest flat, 2.25 root width.
The tail (r 9.8 – 10.4) is inside the neck wall so the tooth fuses into the bottle; the sloped sides are the 60° flanks.
The tooth is only 1.6 mm wide: press Fit in the sketch toolbar or scroll to zoom on the neck zone. Names on shows L1 … L11; select a line and press F2 to give it your own name (e.g. AXIS).
steps.why: This sketch IS the thread. Everything it needs is visible: the axis it turns about, the root and crest radii, where on the part it starts, and the pitch. Change a dimension and the whole helix follows.

checkpoint.expected: A small closed tooth, its dashed amber guide lines (L1 – L5) and eight dimensions, in the neck zone.

steps.title: Sweep the tooth along a helix (bottle thread)
instructions: Part+ › Threads & coils › Thread from sketch.
Profile = Bottle thread tooth. Thread axis = L1 · construction line of that sketch. Operation = Join, Solid = Bottle.
Pitch 3, turns 5, right-hand, start angle 0 (the tooth starts exactly where it is drawn).
Tolerance: type  clr  (linked to the global parameter = 0.15 mm).
While the dialog is open the model shows the axis (cyan, named), the start tooth (yellow) and the helix path (orange). Select the feature in the timeline later to see them again.
steps.why: The tooth turns 360° per pitch about the axis line while rising 3 mm. With the tolerance, it is made 0.15 mm smaller on every side than the nominal tooth, which is the gap the printer needs.

checkpoint.expected: A five-turn helical ridge fused to the neck; one body.

instructions: Sketch on the XZ plane. The cap is drawn 22.5 mm above the bottle so both parts stay visible.

FIRST the construction axis: (0,150) → (0,172.5) [L1]. Then one closed outline, (radius, height): bore (12,150) → (15.5,150) → (15.5,170.5) → 2 mm corner arc → (13.5,172.5) → (0,172.5) → (0,170) → (12,170) → close.

steps.title: Revolve the cap about its axis line
instructions: Revolve → Profile = Cap profile, Axis = L1 · construction line, 360°.
Operation = New, so the cap is a separate body (it is coloured orange).
steps.why: A separate body can be moved, hidden or exported on its own, and printed as its own part.

steps.title: Grip flutes with Pattern+
instructions: Create the flute cutter: a Ø2 × 18 cylinder standing on the cap rim at (15.5, 0, 150) (Solid › Cylinder, 12 facets).
Part+ › Patterns › Pattern+. Seed = the cutter, Layout = Round an axis, Axis = World +Z through the origin, Copies = 20, Total angle 360°, Copies turn with the pattern.
Result = Cut from a target body, Target = Cap, leave “Keep the seed” off. The cutter is consumed.

Select the cap's round side face first and the axis is taken from it automatically (“Axis of the round face I selected”): the same dialog also builds grids on any flat face or sketch plane, and with a Rise per copy it makes a helix.
steps.why: One cutter, one dialog: the same Pattern+ repeats a body in any plane or round any axis. Doing this BEFORE the thread keeps the cap simple for the boolean.

steps.title: Sketch the cap thread tooth (referenced to the axis)

courses.title: Electric Kettle: Body, Spout and Handle
courses.objective: Loft a kettle body, close the base, split off the lid band, build a domed lid, pipe a tapering spout and cut its inlet, pipe a handle, analyse the surfaces and thicken everything.

steps.title: Body sections
steps.learn: Five circles from the Ø148 base, out to Ø160 at the belly, in to Ø108 at the lid.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XY at Z 0, 30, 110, 170 and 195: circles Ø148, Ø160, Ø148, Ø120, Ø108.
Start each circle at the back (−X), where the handle will hide the seam.
steps.why: The belly low down gives stability and volume; the narrow top keeps the lid small. A closed surface has a seam where its curves start — put it where it does not matter.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the body
steps.learn: Loft base to top.
instructions: NURBS › Loft, degree 3.
steps.why: One smooth body surface.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Close the base
steps.learn: Flat N-sided fill on the base circle.
instructions: NURBS+ › N-sided: base circle, flat.
steps.why: A flat base so the kettle stands on its power plate.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Split off the lid band
steps.learn: Split the body at 92 % of its height. The top band becomes part of the lid.
instructions: NURBS › Split: body, direction v, at 0.92.
steps.why: A split gives two surfaces that still meet exactly, like a real lid gap.

checkpoint.expected: Body and a separate narrow band at the top.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Domed lid
steps.learn: Loft the lid dome from the top rim to a small knob.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XY: Ø108 at Z 195, Ø88 at 203, Ø52 at 209, Ø16 at 212.
NURBS › Loft.
steps.why: The dome starts on the same circle as the body top, so it fits exactly.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Spout
steps.learn: Pipe a spout that tapers from Ø32 to Ø14 along a rising curve.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ: spline from (60, 50) up and out to (150, 190).
NURBS › Pipe: radius 16 → 7.
steps.why: A tapered pipe gives the spout its draught-free nose. It starts inside the body so the two overlap.

checkpoint.expected: A spout rising from the front.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Spout inlet
steps.learn: Cut the hole where the water enters the spout.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on YZ at X 200 (in front of the kettle): circle Ø22 at (0, 72).
NURBS+ › Trim: body, −X, keep outside.
steps.why: Water needs a way in. Projecting from the front along −X puts the hole on the front wall only.

checkpoint.expected: A hole in the front of the body behind the spout.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Handle
steps.learn: Pipe a Ø22 handle along a C-shaped path at the back.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ: spline from (−66, 165) out to (−118, 110) and back to (−76, 45).
NURBS › Pipe: radius 11.
steps.why: The ends sink into the body, giving a firm grip area away from the hot wall.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.learn: Zebra and comb on everything.
instructions: NURBS+ › Zebra and Comb.
steps.why: Check the belly and the lid: stripes should run smoothly from body into lid band and dome.

checkpoint.expected: Smooth stripes on body and lid.

NURBS › Thicken each surface.
steps.why: All parts become solids you can section and weigh.

checkpoint.expected: A solid kettle: body, lid band, dome, spout and handle.
